title: Double Circulation in the Human Heart
subject: biology
learningObjectives: Identify the 4 chambers of the human heart (Right Atrium, Right Ventricle, Left Atrium, Left Ventricle).
Trace the deoxygenated blood pathway from Vena Cava through the Right Heart to the Pulmonary Artery and Lungs.
Trace the oxygenated blood pathway from Pulmonary Veins through the Left Heart to the Aorta and Body.
Understand why mammalian circulation is called 'Double Circulation' (Pulmonary and Systemic circuits).
Observe how heart valves prevent the backflow of blood during systole and diastole.

scenes.purpose: Establish the 3D heart anatomy, identifying the 4 chambers, great vessels, and pericardial orientation.
Trace deoxygenated blood flow from superior/inferior vena cava into the right atrium, right ventricle, and through the pulmonary arteries to the lungs.
Trace oxygen-rich blood returning via pulmonary veins into the left atrium, thick muscular left ventricle, and pumped through the aorta into systemic circulation.
Visualize the coordinated action of tricuspid, bicuspid (mitral), and semilunar valves during cardiac cycle (systole and diastole).
Consolidate the concept of double circulation with circuit flow schematic and summary.
